revisions.note: Geometry contract untouched (protected A32 asset): ten zones, S10+ portrait [9,10], padding_dp 6, same storage and same preset names. Three real defects fixed: (1) A32's one-way push moved clusters off the panel / left them inside the excluded interval, so A33 solves against the free intervals; (2) applyLayout measured before resetting the previous transform, so it drifted on every render - it is now idempotent; (3) the Settings safe-zone editor carried a second copy of the placement arithmetic that still had defect (1), so its preview disagreed with the real bar - the planner is now a single exported function used by both, with an honest 'preview needs the launcher engine' message when it is absent. VM-verifiable (ceiling VERIFIED_IN_VM_ONLY); on-glass verdict NEEDS_OWNER_TEST.

revisions.note: Revision 3 (bg-02 verification pass) - protected-geometry re-verification, no change to the ten-zone contract and no rewrite of the A32 preset: ZONES=10, S10+ portrait blocks [9,10] (the dual-punch cutout), padding_dp 6, and the same storage name/document, all re-checked by the suite (44 checks, 0 failures) and by the INV-3 hard assertions. The A32 preset file configs/nuxel/statusbar-safezones.json is byte-identical (5dec2d29...) because the correct action for a protected asset is to verify its hash, not to edit it. What is added here is evidence and owner-facing completeness: (a) the SAFE-ZONES document now carries the explicit per-zone geometry table for the real 1440x3040 panel in portrait (W=1440) AND landscape (W=3040) with raw and clamped intervals, showing numerically that padded zones 9 and 10 merge into one blocked interval 1140..1440 and leave the right cluster the single free interval 0..1140 - i.e. blocked regions EXCLUDE status items rather than being painted over them; (b) the landscape presets are empty on S10+ with the reason stated (the punch-hole is on the short edge, so nothing sits above the bar when it rotates), and the centre/left/right/none presets plus the live-preview/persistence/overflow behaviour of the Settings editor are asserted by the same suite; (c) overflow is reported (dropped: no_free_interval) rather than drawn inside the cutout, and the profile is keyed on the real hardware identity so a Pixel-style centred camera is a forward-compatible profile rather than an assumption. On-glass status-bar evidence stays NEEDS_OWNER_TEST.
